result.notes: Checks that passed, with no finding. Both workflow files parse (yaml.safe_load). The wait-step test (python -m unittest tests.test_site -k wait_step) ran 1 test, OK, in 10.6 s. The CI unit step for the website modules (test_site, test_gridded, test_basemap, test_storm, test_satellite, test_hail, test_website_workflow) ran 550 tests, OK, with no skips, in 121 s; log at /home/user/hail-b1/out/review-live2/reviewer/ci-unit.log. gh 2.89.0 accepts each flag the workflows use (run list --commit/--json/--jq, release edit --notes, release upload --clobber, release delete-asset with --yes). The jq string gives 'null null' for an empty list and 'completed <conclusion>' otherwise. The wait step, run as bash -e <file>, exits 0 on every path on main. On a branch it exits 1 when a store job ran and did not succeed, and exits 0 when no store job exists for the commit. The 40-check bound is exact. Only a branch named exactly main can produce main's name, so no branch build reads or writes it. On day as_of+4, main records the hail row as not ok, the sheets show the stale line, and the build still exits 0 and deploys. First main build: the merge push starts the store job and the website build together (both path filters match). hail-store-main.tar.gz does not exist yet (HEAD 404 today). If the store job succeeds in time, the build reads it; otherwise the build records the history as unavailable. main's B1 store is about 4,600 files and 36.7 MB uncompressed, inside the B1 reader limits (hail.py lines 769-770); the Pages copy takes only hail/. The wait is needed: claude/hail-b3 website attempt 1 (run 39355361294) failed at 'Build from live data' at 01:50 UTC while its store job ran (01:47:18 to 02:22:57).
